guard: a terminal reported to the emitter is placed on the last turn the source had begun at the position it was reported at, the open run when none was; one placed on a run is owed to it until a frame carrying that run's terminal freezes, and the owed error is published in place of the first finish the mapper produces for the run, in a frame of that run whose cursor stays ahead of the record the finish came from; a repeated terminal, one for a closed run, and one for a turn that opened no run close nothing
why: A turn that failed while its terminal could not be written is owed an error terminal. When the
plane comes back with the next prompt already among the unread records, that prompt's mapping
closes the failed run as a finish; the emitter must publish the owed error in that finish's
place, or the failed turn is recorded as finished (Sol, round 5 of PR 3836, through the built MCP
entry point). The error names no run, so it must travel in a frame of the FAILED run, or it is
labelled as the next run's (Sol, round 6). O1 publishes the synthesized finish as mapped. O2
leaves the debt standing after a close settles the run, so the next debt is refused as a second
one. O3 puts the error in the prompt's own unit, where the frame names the next run. O4 stores
the prompt's cursor on the owed frame, so an acknowledged error and an unacknowledged prompt
re-read past the prompt and lose the run it opens.
O5 places every terminal on the last turn the read began, whatever position it was reported at.
O6 places nothing. O7 does not count a turn that opened no run. O8 lets a repeated terminal replace
the one its turn has. O9 owes a terminal to a run the wire has closed. O10 settles the successor's
debt when the frame carrying its predecessor's finish freezes. O11 takes the debt at the mapping,
so a frame that fails before the freeze takes the error with it. O12 advances the brackets before
the freeze, so a run whose first frame never froze is reported open (Sol, round 11).
O13 commits a trailing turn only after every publish, so a failure after the freeze carries a stale last turn (Sol, round 12).

mutations.name: O1 the owed terminal is never applied: the synthesized finish is published as mapped
mutations.note: The round-5 defect as the wire saw it: one RUN_FINISHED for the failed run and no RUN_ERROR.

mutations.name: O2 a taken debt stays owed
mutations.note: A debt that outlives its taking is handed back to the next emitter by a dying one and placed again, or refused as a second debt on the next terminal for that run.

mutations.name: O3 the owed error travels in the prompt's unit: the frame names the next run
mutations.note: The round-6 defect as the wire saw it: the failed run's only error labelled with the next run's id.

mutations.name: O4 the owed frame stores the prompt's cursor instead of the position ahead of it
mutations.note: A cursor past the prompt on the owed frame would, once that frame is acknowledged and the prompt's is not, re-read from after the prompt and drop the run it opens.

mutations.name: O5 every terminal is placed on the last turn the read began, whatever its position
mutations.find: for (const [i, t] of begun) if (i < before) turn = t;
mutations.replace: for (const [, t] of begun) turn = t;
mutations.note: A terminal reported before the next prompt was written is placed on that prompt's run, and the run it ended closes as the finish the prompt synthesizes.

mutations.name: O6 a terminal is placed on no turn
mutations.note: The round-10 defect as the emitter would reproduce it: the second turn's run is never owed its terminal.

mutations.name: O7 a turn that opened no run is not counted as a turn
mutations.note: Not counted, the notification's terminal is the run's begun before it: with that run owing nothing yet, the finish is placed on it and closes it. With the run already owed its own terminal the finish is refused as a repeat instead, which is why the earlier notification cell cannot see this mutation.

mutations.name: O8 a repeated terminal replaces the one its turn has
mutations.find: if (turn === undefined || turn === null || this.owed.has(turn)) continue;
mutations.note: The live seat sends a stop after a stop failure for the same turn; the later finish would replace the error.

mutations.name: O9 a terminal for a run the wire has closed is owed to it
mutations.note: A debt to a closed run is never settled and is refused as a second one, or applied to a finish the run never had.

mutations.name: O10 a freeze settles the debt of the run the frame is labelled with, not the run the finish closes
mutations.note: The finish the next prompt synthesizes for its predecessor travels in the successor's frame; settled by label, the successor's own terminal is lost and the prompt after it closes the failed run as a finish.

mutations.name: O11 the debt is taken at the mapping, before the frame carrying it freezes
mutations.find:
const { terminal } = this.owed.get(runId)!;
    if (!terminal.error) return undefined;
mutations.note: The round-11 defect: a log write refused once while the owed error was being written took the error with it, and the next recovery closed the failed run as a finish.

mutations.name: O12 the brackets advance before the freeze
mutations.find:
await this.wal.beginSend({ id, E, seq: frame.seq, sourceCursor: cursor, body, brackets });
    this.brackets = next;
mutations.replace:
this.brackets = next;
    await this.wal.beginSend({ id, E, seq: frame.seq, sourceCursor: cursor, body, brackets });
mutations.note: The round-11 defect: a first turn whose frame never froze was reported open, its terminal held for a run the fresh start never had, and dropped.

mutations.name: O13 a trailing turn is committed only after every publish, not with the frame that consumes it
mutations.note: The round-12 defect: a fold refused after the ack left the last turn at the human run while the log was past the notification, and the notification's stop closed that run as a finish on the next emitter.

mutations.name: O14 a terminal ahead of a gap the read stepped over is held for a record that never comes
mutations.find: if (first === undefined) return ahead.cursor === read.cursor ? read.records.length : undefined;
mutations.note: The round-13 defect: a torn line written past the position a terminal was reported at, while the plane was down, left the terminal waiting after the re-establish; the settle pumped without end and the run was never closed.
